cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Changed the Odds
cards.instruction: Hide how your own choice tilted the contest, bargain, or consequence while continuing to judge the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. A fair result. Let's celebrate my cake's first prize.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why did you move yours under the judging light?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Lighting maintenance. We shouldn't let logistics overshadow flavour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine was left in the shade.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A useful note for whoever organises next year's logistics.

mechanism: A assumes authority to certify the outcome and uses that position to dismiss inquiry into A own advantage-changing choice as logistics or inadmissible testing.
confusable: D181 distributes blame after a problem; D205 specifically hides A intervention in odds while continuing to judge the resulting contest.
comparison: Cake placement changes judging exposure and is moved to future logistics; folded raffle ticket makes selection recognizable and is shielded by results-chair authority.
seedUse: Both exact cards and all four canonical seeds read. Preserve B explicit personal intervention; do not treat A fairness declaration as verified evidence.
